newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical starts laser surgery trial.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical starts laser surgery trial.

text.p: U.S. Surgical Corp said Monday it had begun clinical tests of a laser device for a surgical procedure that creats pathways in the heart to allow blood to reach oxygen-starved tissue in patients with coronary artery problems.
Surgical said a surgeon used the device in an operation on a 75-year-old man at Loma Linda University Medical Center in Loma Linda, California on September 2.
The surgery is known as transmyocardial revascularization, or TMR, it added.
Surgical said more trials will begin at University of Washington in Seattle and Allegheny University of the Health Sciences in Philadelphia.
U.S. Surgical said the surgeon who worked on the patient called the operation a success.

"He received four coronary artery bypass grafts, and 10 laser channels were created on the side of his heart," it quoted Steven Gundry as saying. "He was discharged after only three days in the hopsital. The area of his heart muscle which received TMR had already improved function."
